text: Operator opened with conversation-only; design talked through over 11 turns before any action
lesson: conversation-first surfaces direction cheaply; save it to memory as it lands

text: Measured the current learning loop before designing the new one: 581 hub feedback msgs, 150/188 asks open, farming last ran 2026-09-14 with 0 recurrences
lesson: measure before designing; numbers turned a feeling into a finding

text: Operator ceased investment in the old harness; stop AP/Conductor pickups without disrupting operations
lesson: freeze the old wheel before building the new

text: Drain-then-stop: paused launch crons, let in-flight runs finish, watcher raises stop flag at zero children, 3h cap
lesson: stop pickups without killing work; one switch afterwards

text: crontab <file> with a very long scratchpad path failed (path truncated); fixed by crontab - < file
lesson: install crontabs via stdin; verify with diff after

text: Paused 2 launch paths but the wheel clock (launchSpoke/orchestrator-wilbur) started a new run
lesson: inventory EVERY launch path before claiming pickups are stopped; a seed Governor scenario

text: agent-tool-scope-guard refused subagent prompts containing the words read-only
lesson: guards keyed on prose wording cost a retry; describe the deliverable, not a restriction

text: bash-lug-guard false positive: heredoc text mentioning lugs/docs blocked a memory write
lesson: regex guards on command text misfire; use Edit for prose writes

text: Operator redirected to assimilate prior art first; two parallel subagents (web prior art + own hf bootstrap excavation)
lesson: assimilate before invent; parallel research keeps the main context lean

text: hf bootstrap was never run by a stranger or on a clean box; only proof is a fake-claude fixture; sanitizing never built
lesson: anti-pattern: proof by fake fixture; seed scenario requires a real signed-in agent on a clean machine

text: No prior art does fleet learning, calibration of self-assessment, or migration by rebuild; ETH study: always-loaded context files raise cost >20%
lesson: borrow the frame, keep the evidence layer as ours; keep always-loaded text minimal

text: Operator: event-log the genesis process to learn patterns and anti-patterns
lesson: the journal becomes seed/journal/ and every incarnation keeps one

text: Operator: the prior-art map names our offer to a stranger -- the management of layers; Wheelwright is an evolution of what was already available
lesson: others ship one layer; we compose, size, evolve and migrate the layers with evidence

text: Operator: managing a layer includes managing its MEMORY and knowing when the layer becomes a bottleneck and needs to change
lesson: every layer carries a health signal (cost per use, queue growth, staleness, ignored rules, workarounds); crossing it triggers a change nomination

text: Operator go: seed repo created with README, AGENTS.md, llms.txt, START, CHARTER v0.1.0, OUTLINE, journal, bootstrap scar source
lesson: the first commit carries its own journal

text: bash-destructive-command-guard matched > README.md against the cwd file of the same name, though the target was a new repo
lesson: guards that resolve relative paths against the wrong cwd misfire; write new files with the Write tool

text: Subagent dispatched to write into the new seed repo was refused by the old harness's agent-target-scope-guard: the seed is not a registered repo and no dispatch-time grant was written
lesson: grant write scope to a new repo at dispatch time, before the subagent starts; a fork cannot grant itself scope and must not route around the guard

text: Blocked subagent drafted all files in its scratchpad and handed back the copy and commit steps instead of stopping empty-handed
lesson: when a write is blocked, finish the work in an allowed place and raise the block with the exact next step

text: Charter V (records travel) and the no-personal-detail rule pull against each other: identity and machine facts must stay out of tracked files, yet records must survive migration
lesson: split records: tracked steering plus ledger travel; identity and environment live in an untracked .local/ that is short and re-asked or re-derived on each machine

text: Each scenario carries a FALSIFIABILITY line naming the concrete change that turns it red
lesson: a check no change could fail checks nothing; write the falsifier before the check steps

text: Hub build tasks name what to observe, not which command to type
lesson: environment-neutral proof: the agent picks the native command for the OS it reported

text: Old harness: 45 of 63 review lugs were refused because the top independence bar (a different provider) was unreachable; the bar was then tiered by priority
lesson: a review bar nobody can reach becomes a queue, not a gate; tier independence by priority, never waive it

text: Old harness: certification fired before the work was merged and produced nine false FAILED verdicts; another verdict failed because evidence was truncated from 320KB to 131KB
lesson: certify what ships, and make proof fit the reviewer's input budget

text: Old harness ready bar: each block reason was backtested against 76 real runs (base wasted rate 66%); a reason blocks only if it beats the base rate by 15+ points, else it only warns
lesson: decide block versus warn from measured outcomes, not intuition; recount when numbers move

text: Old harness: 276 open lugs in 10 spokes asked for another spoke's code; 204 sat untouched for 14 days
lesson: a lug lives where its files are; cross-spoke work is a communication lug, and a re-homed lug is triaged at home

text: Old harness stage-owner table started in warn mode: each lug move has an owner, and the same actor moving two stages in a row is recorded before it is ever refused
lesson: introduce a new rule as a measured warning; enforce once the data shows it holds

text: Old harness lug schema grew to 51KB across five types, with states nobody set
lesson: states nobody will set are the failure mode; the seed keeps two types and a trivial lug needs four fields

text: Old harness advisors each carried a counter-metric (a certifier counts reopen-after-pass) and registered a first baseline openly when none existed
lesson: every advisor needs a harm number beside its success number; null beats a plausible guess

text: Seed CORE.md and the lugs and advisors skills were written by a dispatched subagent, but the dispatch scope guard refused its writes to the seed repo; files were staged in scratch for the parent to land
lesson: a fork's write scope is set by its dispatcher; grant the target repo at dispatch, or the fork stages and hands back

text: Both parallel builders were refused writes to the new seed repo by the scope guard (unregistered repo, no grant at dispatch); main session surfaced it and landed only after the operator said to
lesson: grant helper scope before dispatch; a blocked write is finished elsewhere and raised, never routed around (now in START)

text: Builder invented a meaning for tread pattern; operator meaning is the feature fingerprint drawn as a picture; corrected in CORE
lesson: undefined terms get invented; every glossary term needs the operator meaning before helpers use it

text: Operator: register it. Seed registered with the operator's other repos so dispatched builders can write to it
lesson: register a new repo before dispatching builders into it

text: Outline doubted Kiro's auto inclusion mode; the live docs show four real modes (always, fileMatch, manual, auto) and auto needs both name and description, which the seed's steering files lacked
lesson: check prior-art claims against the live source before fixing; the doubt was wrong but surfaced a real missing field

text: Charter governance says every amendment names its failing scenario, but the 0.1.1 V/VII clarification came from builder feedback with no scenario run red
lesson: a PATCH clarification has no failing scenario by nature; either exempt PATCH or say so in the sync note (done: 'none run red')

text: Excavation must 'read locally, nothing leaves', yet sifting with a cloud model sends content to its provider
lesson: 'nothing leaves' means nothing beyond a model the user's mandates already allow for that content; say it in the rule, offer a local model

text: Engagement moments written as trigger, ask, record, with triggers read from records rather than hunches, and 'later' recorded as unset with the moment that will need it
lesson: a curriculum is testable when every moment names an observable trigger and a record it writes

text: skill-creator's SKILL.md mentions an 'assertions' field, but its references/schemas.md names the evals.json list 'expectations' (plain strings); grading.json uses text/passed/evidence exactly
lesson: read the schema file, not the prose summary; field names are the contract a viewer depends on

text: CORE's ledger kinds have no 'prediction'; the calibration survey records the prediction as an evidence row whose subject is the survey id
lesson: a record shape with a closed enum needs every later skill checked against it; add a kind or name the mapping

text: Temporary boundary expiry written as 'every reader checks expires.at; past it the value IS reverts_to' instead of a timer
lesson: a self-enforcing expiry is a read-time rule, never a background wait or a remembered promise

text: Stop switch given three positions (run, drain, stop) so drain-then-stop needs only one switch every launch path checks
lesson: one switch with a drain position beats two switches; lowering it is a loosening and needs the user's yes

text: Engagement guide loads skills/governor at stage 3 (trust earned), but boundaries are written at stage 0 in mandates.md; 'group' is used for funding with no CORE glossary entry
lesson: a skill's first moment must match the earliest stage that writes its records; new terms go in CORE before skills use them

text: Operator: patch exempt. Charter 0.2.0: PATCH (wording only) exempt from the failing-scenario rule; MAJOR/MINOR still need one
lesson: a rule nobody can satisfy for honest clarifications gets amended, with the failed case as its evidence

text: Operator to sleep: build the seed out completely and test it before applying to live projects; overnight plan written to journal/overnight-plan-2026-11-05.md; trials isolated in the registered seed-trials repo
lesson: write the night plan into the repo before starting so a context reset cannot lose it

text: Tread rendering rule test-rendered to SVG and rasterized: geometry correct, but a standalone converter ignored currentColor and drew no rings or labels
lesson: a rendering rule is proven only by rendering it; theme-neutral currentColor needs a stated fallback for converters outside a page

text: Tread modules listed in a fixed order and fixed length, unused ones at depth none, local modules appended sorted
lesson: comparison needs alignment by construction: never let a fingerprint drop empty slots to look cleaner

text: Sharing offer shows the whole scanned package and one yes approves exactly that text; any change needs a new yes
lesson: easy sharing and user-reads-before-it-leaves reconcile when the consent is attached to the exact text, not to the intent

text: Parallel builder edited OUTLINE.md at the same time; only this builder's one line was staged by writing a blob from HEAD plus that line
lesson: when two builders share a file, stage a constructed blob of your own hunk; never git add the whole file

text: skills/sharing-flavors defines flavor and item, and skills/tread defines a hub tread/ folder, but CORE has no flavor/item glossary entries and hub/DESIGN's layout has no tread/
lesson: new terms and new hub folders belong in CORE and DESIGN before skills rely on them; file the follow-up when another builder owns those files

text: Calibration survey wrote predictions as evidence rows; CORE now has a prediction kind and the verdict row names the prediction it answers
lesson: a measurement that depends on order (predict before grade) deserves its own record kind, so a grader can find it without reading its content

text: Release-only checks marked per expectation in evals.json (release_only: expectation + proxy), not per scenario, and the scenario step says 'Release only' with the same proxy
lesson: split tiers at the check, not the scenario: most of a costly scenario is cheap, and a proxy pass is evidence, never a release

text: Stranger read found the governor listing seven boundary kinds while the Charter, CORE, DESIGN and mandates.md listed six (no time)
lesson: when a skill extends a list the Charter states, update every copy at once or flag the Charter for a PATCH; lists drift silently

text: START named only two skills' moments, so an agent starting from START alone would never load engagement-guide, governor or excavation-migration at the first conversation
lesson: the bootstrap MUST name every skill's moment; a skill the entry file never points to is invisible to a prose-only reader

text: A harness guard blocked a python edit to skills/lugs/SKILL.md because the path contains lugs/; the Edit tool landed it
lesson: prose paths can collide with a host's record-path heuristics; use a narrower write tool rather than disputing or routing around the guard

text: Independent review: the first meeting told the builder to record answers in steering files, ledger and schedule, while START and R3 say nothing is written before the plan is agreed
lesson: a skill's 'what to record' must say when the write is allowed; hold answers until the build task that writes them

text: Independent review: lugs were tagged stage 0 in CORE but START, lugs and engagement-guide start them at stage 1; excavation 'revive' and retro follow-ups pointed at lugs at stage 0
lesson: one stage tag per term, then grep every use; give stage 0 a landing place (goals.md, records.md open items)

text: Independent review: Charter IV listed six boundary kinds while governor, CORE and mandates.md listed seven (time); Charter bumped 0.2.0 -> 0.2.1 as a PATCH
lesson: a list the Charter states and a skill extends is a drift risk; fix the Charter by PATCH

text: Independent review: sharing-flavors said the user decides before stage 2, advisors said the hub decides; nominations were filed as lugs at stage 0
lesson: state who decides per stage in every skill that mentions the loop: before stage 2 the hub agent runs it and the user decides

text: Independent review: hub AGENTS.md pointed at START.md that the hub does not hold (only seed/START.md); stop switch file and tread/ folder had no place in the hub layout; ledger field names differed between CORE and DESIGN
lesson: every pointer inside a built hub must resolve inside the hub; name every file a skill tells the agent to create

text: Independent review: the journal carried internal tool and repo names into a seed that gets copied into every hub; scrubbed
lesson: a seed ships to strangers; scan the journal as well as the instructions

text: Independent review: START never said to keep the seed read-only, where the hub goes, who grades, or to run the Charter Check; 'wheel', 'seed', 'lift', 'incarnation' were used but never defined
lesson: list the actions a builder must not guess: where to write, who checks, which gate to run; define every word the vocabulary leans on

text: Drain-then-stop completed: last old-harness run finished on its own, stop flag raised at 12:47 AM with 0 running children, 11 queued dispatches marked killed, cron lines restored so the flag is the one switch
lesson: draining took 2 hours; a drain needs a visible cap and a visible end state

text: The last old-harness run landed a registry change (hub holds the only known-repos registry); right after, session hooks reported the tastegraph master missing and the inbox count fell from 244 to 4
lesson: a change that lands during a freeze can still shift live behavior; check the last landing before trusting the board

text: Gen 1 haiku graded 6 of 17 (31 of 54 expectations) vs predicted 14: calibration error +8, all misses overconfident. Ledger timestamps were invented in a batch.
lesson: self-prediction from a small model is badly overconfident; the seed must demand real event times and proof rows with verbatim timed output

text: After the final old-harness landing (hub-only registry), a worktree session resolves the hub registry to a nonexistent sibling path (.local/worktrees/wheel-hub), so the scope guard refused the grader; registering there unblocked it
lesson: a registry move must be tested from worktrees too; old-harness bug to report, not fix, during the freeze

text: Gen 1 sonnet graded 8 of 17 vs predicted 15 (+7 overconfident). Both models failed the same seven areas: visible footing/plan/defaults before writes, proof record, evidence bundle, machine launch-path survey, ledger row after a yes, builder done-claims, re-entry answer shape
lesson: failures shared across models point at the seed, not the builder: fix the seed first

text: Seed fix pass from gen 1 grades (a85db84): stand-in runs defined and made visible-before-write; scratch-area rule for pre-yes writes; event-time rule and proof-row shape in CORE; build tasks for before/after records, proof row and evidence bundle; AGENTS and environment templates; evals 001/002/004/005/006/008/009/011/012/013/014/015/016 fixed and scenario files synced
lesson: rules a later session needs at runtime belong in the hub's own pointer file, not only in a skill that is never loaded by default

text: Both builders hid the first conversation inside their own reasoning and wrote ledger rows in one late batch; the seed had said 'interactive' and 'nothing is written' without defining either
lesson: a word a builder must act on (interactive, write, done, time) needs a one-line definition where it is used, or every model reads it its own way

text: Evals 001 proxy (empty shop), 004 (condition never arose), 011 (live stop on a shared machine) and 013 (vacuous at stage 0) could not discriminate as written
lesson: every expectation must be runnable on the trial as designed; a grader-run side session on a copy is cheaper than an expectation nobody can meet

text: Gen 2 haiku graded 7 of 17 (was 6) vs predicted 15 (+8 overconfident). Fixed: 004, 006, 008. Regressed: 005 and 014 (no git, so nothing proves .local/ is ignored or the ledger is tracked), 015 (head -10 truncated the timer list). 009 and 012 yes-paths cannot be delivered by an agent grader.
lesson: calibration did not improve between generations; the seed must name how to verify sign-in, require a tracking tool or an equivalent proof, and forbid truncated listings; trial design needs a card-driven yes the hub reads itself

text: Gen 2 sonnet graded 10 of 17 (was 8) vs predicted 16 (+6). Proof board written to journal/PROOF-BOARD.md. New risk: fresh hub sessions tried a user-level connector that would send notes to an outside service against the mandate; the permission layer refused
lesson: inherited global tools must be checked against the hub mandates; self-prediction stays overconfident across models and generations

text: Seed fix pass from gen 2 grades (46bd1f1): one defaults list printed and recorded unchanged; every launch-path kind listed in full and the before record saved in scratch before the yes, copied unchanged; ledger times copied from a printed clock reading, boundary rows carry evidence; bundle pointers checked by id lookup; sign-in check defined; tracking proof for git and no-git; inherited tools checked against mandates (R23, scenario 018); stand-in cards for 009/012 yes paths; grader filters whole transcript events; model lanes frontier|fast|local; R7 names .env-style files
lesson: a rule a builder keeps breaking needs a mechanical pattern (one list, one clock read, one id lookup), not a stronger word

text: Gen 2 failures clustered where the seed said what to achieve but not how to check it: defaults matched by memory, times typed by hand, pointers checked by pattern, listings cut with head, sign-in called unverifiable
lesson: pair each MUST with the observation that proves it, done by the builder before hand-off

text: A line-level filter for the forecast leaked a multi-line forecast table to the grader; a grader-relayed yes was correctly refused by fresh hub sessions
lesson: filter whole events, not lines; deliver trial answers through a card the hub session reads itself

text: Gen 3 haiku graded 6 of 18 vs predicted 16 (+10). The main session withheld the build transcript from the gen 3 graders to protect independence; under the rule that unreadable evidence fails, six scenarios failed partly or wholly on that alone
lesson: independence must come from filtering the transcript, not withholding it; a trial design choice can masquerade as a seed regression

text: Night run stopped after generation 3 (sonnet 5/18, haiku 6/18, not comparable). Seed grew and evals tightened while scores stayed 5-10; further iteration tonight would not pay. Proof board updated with the verdict and four next steps for the operator
lesson: know when to stop: when each round changes both the seed and the ruler, freeze the ruler before iterating again

text: Operator-approved fixes landed (6b1de90): evals.json frozen as ruler v1 for generations 4 and 5, with a Ruler section in scenarios/README.md and journal/ruler-v2-notes.md for problems found meanwhile; two impossible expectations fixed at the freeze (013 #1 vs build task 8 rows, 014 #3 proxy vs scratch-note rows)
lesson: freeze the ruler before iterating the seed, so a score change means the seed changed

text: Grader independence now comes from a filtered transcript the orchestrator makes mechanically (marker list, whole-event stubs that keep line, timestamp and type, ledger and checklist reductions, hub and scratch copies), never from withholding it; a grading without it is not a valid run
lesson: write a filter precisely enough that a script implements it, then check it with one

text: START rewritten as an ordered checklist the builder ticks with clock-stamped output (830 -> 446 words); each tick appends {step, at, status, evidence} to proof/checklist.jsonl and the step's ledger rows with the same clock value; explanations moved to hub/DESIGN.md (The tick, Working rules)
lesson: the four never-passed areas each got one mechanical step: one call prints and records defaults, survey evidence counts every kind, rows are written by the tick at their event, the question is printed before the card is read

text: A tick is called ticked, never done: the seed reserves done for a checker's verdict, so the checklist status vocabulary is ticked | blocked
lesson: check a new record's words against the seed's reserved words before adopting an example verbatim

text: Seed gains the work board (856e6cf): board/BOARD.md generated from lugs, initiatives, the ledger, proof/checklist.jsonl and verdict rows, never edited; five sections (Where we stand, Achieved, Planned, Errors, Activity); every number links to its record; SHOULD regenerate on every ledger append, MUST at each session end; markdown always, self-contained HTML optional, no server; no personal detail. Defined in skills/lugs/references/board.md, summarized in skills/lugs section 9
lesson: observability is a view of the records, not a second record: generate it, never hand-write it, so it cannot drift from the truth

text: Board stage placement: at stage 0 it shows the hub's records (goals, open items, checklist, ledger errors); from stage 1 it shows lugs. hub/DESIGN.md layout gains board/ but no build task or checklist step, so the frozen ruler's builds stay comparable; engagement-guide 6.1 introduces it at the first spoke; CORE glossary adds board
lesson: add a new behavior beside the frozen checklist, not inside it, and park its scenario in ruler-v2-notes

text: The board shows only what is recorded, so refusals, blocks and breaches must be written as ledger rows when they happen; a board stamp naming the last ledger row lets any reader see it is stale
lesson: a dashboard's error section is only as good as the habit of recording errors at their event

text: Charter 0.3.0 (b8527f4), MINOR: adds VIII. Plan big, build small (plans, specs and lugs written by a capable model MUST be executable by a smaller, cheaper, faster one without further reasoning; a step a small model cannot carry out is a plan defect, fixed in the plan first) and IX. Measure it or it does not count (every change, lever and claim MUST name its measure and baseline before it is made, and its movement is shown afterward). Evidence: haiku below sonnet on the same seed in both comparable rounds (gen 1 6 vs 8, gen 2 7 vs 10 of 17); levers 6b1de90 and 856e6cf pulled with no measure; calibration error +6 to +11
lesson: a principle enters the Charter with the trial numbers that show the seed breaking it today, so its fix can be measured against the same numbers

text: Reflected lightly: CORE glossary gains measure and lever, model lane gains one line (plans written for the fast lane), Charter Check gains questions 8 and 9; ruler-v2-notes gains candidate scenarios small-model parity and every lever names its measure; START (446 words) and evals.json unchanged
lesson: the next lever (round 4) must name its measure and baseline before it is pulled, or it repeats the turn 54 and 56 gap that IX now forbids

text: Round 4 sonnet (ruler v1, first clean read): 8 of 18 (45/59 expectations) vs predicted 17 (+9). New passes vs round 3: 001, 004, 013, 015. Still failing: 002, 005, 008, 009, 010, 011, 012, 014, 016, 018.
lesson: the stamped checklist moved the proof and overwrite scenarios; defaults, launch paths and question-before-card still fail on the seed side

text: Orchestrator mistakes in round 4: filter_transcript.py removed 31 events outright instead of leaving same-line stubs as grader.md requires, and the hub handed to the grader was not a filtered copy (the grader made its own)
lesson: the orchestrator tooling must implement grader.md exactly; build a checked hand-off step, not ad hoc commands

text: Round-5 lever 46a2210 (prose only, ruler v1 untouched): R1 fixed by making the pointer a checked step (footing names the agent's instruction file; task 10 writes AGENTS.md plus an identical CLAUDE.md, cmp-checked; task 12 rehearses re-entry in a fresh process whose first line must read 'Hub rules loaded from <file>.'); grader.md verdict rows go to the hub copy and the hub-copy filter covers board/ and forecast-quoting files; mechanical steps for 010, 011, 009, 012, 008, 005, 014, 015, 016, 018, plus one sentence each for 001 and 002. START 458 words.
lesson: a rule the seed writes into a file the agent never loads is not a rule; every runtime rule needs a fresh-session check that proves it was read

text: Lever note written before the edit (journal/levers.md L5, Charter IX): measure = round 5 scenario pass counts per model on ruler v1; baseline = round 4 sonnet 8/18, haiku 5/18; point forecast sonnet 11/18 (9 to 13), haiku 8/18 (6 to 10), shaded down from the table's expected values (about 12 and 9) for the past +6 to +11 forecast error; per-scenario flip calls recorded
lesson: name which scenarios a lever should flip, so a flip elsewhere is not credited to it and a miss points at the step that failed

text: Judgment-shaped steps replaced with checks a small model can run: exact-substring bundle phrases instead of 'shows what the line says', chmod plus hash instead of 'never edit before.md', a named-line defaults list instead of 'every assumed value', count matches for inherited tools, a fixed first line for the stop answer
lesson: Charter VIII in practice: when two builders miss the same rule, turn the rule into a command whose output shows pass or fail

text: Restart as seed v1, chamber 0 (the nautilus shell). v0.1 (charter 0.3.0, e396898) sealed in archive/v0.1/. New root: CHARTER 1.0.0 (I goals are the alignment, II grow the shell, III smoke test intrinsic, then the earlier principles; mission: recursive self-improvement, transparent and collaborative), START cut loop, SMOKE (S-0-01..S-0-07), GOALS, WORK, BOARD, CHAMBERS.
lesson: when added rules leave scores flat while the seed grows, restart small around the loop, not the feature list

text: Measure of the restart, named before any build: the chamber 0 seal (a fast-lane build from the seed alone, cut 1 sealed, cut 2 through start smoke, a different-session grader re-runs S-0-01..S-0-07, all pass). Baseline: none sealed; v0.1 round 4 ruler v1 haiku 5/18, sonnet 8/18.
lesson: grading the seal on the small model makes plan big, build small a test, not a slogan

text: Helper agents were blocked from writing the chamber 0 branch twice by a wording-keyed scope guard; the main session landed the drafted script under the operator's standing instruction to land blocked builder work, and added S-0-07 from the round 5 hook-leak finding.
lesson: describe a helper's workspace, never a restriction; a dispatch tool that grants scope beats prose

text: Charter 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0 (MINOR): IX becomes 'Presentation is per-user taste, and crafted': what the user sees is designed for their goals and taste with advanced, effective design craft, never a generic template; plain only until the interview records their taste. Failing check: operator feedback that every solution looks alike and the first sprint board was 'not clear what is being conveyed'; v0.1 trials rebuilt boards three times before they read clearly.
lesson: a plain default with no recorded taste ships the same generic look every time; make taste a recorded answer and craft a rule

text: The first cut opens with a specialist interview (GOALS.md, pointer from START step 01): goals (words + measure), direction, budget (money, time, effort as boundaries the wheel never moves on its own), how to see progress (just in time on meaningful events, the board on demand), and taste. Few questions at a time, 'later' is valid, every answer one ledger row with a topic, in the user's words. Then the wheel automates and iterates cut by cut.
lesson: interview before automating: the boundaries and the update cadence are what let the wheel run on its own without surprising the user

text: BOARD.md gains Design craft (summary before detail, one headline per section, charts only where they show movement with a takeaway, state by shape and label not colour alone, scope first, no generic looks, light and dark, phone-readable) and Delivery (just-in-time notices, on-demand board regenerated first). Smoke S-0-08: the latest taste row id appears in the board's stamp line. CHAMBERS: the user's review of each chamber's board against their taste is part of every seal, not a separate chamber. START 356 words.
lesson: keep a taste rule mechanical by making the board name the taste row it rendered with; the review stays human, the link stays checkable

text: First chamber-0 seal test (fast-lane build, stand-in user): the builder ran cut 1 to step 10, found S-0-07 red at end (r-000042), recorded why it could not fix it without the user's yes (r-000044, r-000047), refused to seal and opened cut 2 with the red check carried forward. It stopped instead of faking a seal.
lesson: a seal rule a small model can read mechanically holds under pressure: it is cheaper to stop honestly than to invent a pass when the check, not the builder's judgment, decides

text: S-0-07 contradicted itself for files written by other tools: a global agent hook writes docs/ and runtime/ logs into any folder where an agent session runs, so the check's pass clause ('none unexplained') and red clause ('another tool writes into the wheel') left no green path even after the files were recorded as a finding (r-000028).
lesson: a check must have a reachable green state for every situation it names; name the record that makes a foreign file explained (a foreign row plus the user's ruling), not just the symptom

text: S-0-05 tripped on its own text: its pattern list held literal home-folder paths, so the seed's SMOKE.md copied into a wheel failed the check it defines (r-000017); the builder rewrote the wheel's copy (r-000026).
lesson: a check that searches for a pattern must describe it in words, never as the literal it hunts, or the rule itself becomes the violation

text: S-0-04 had no rule for a board that does not exist yet and the builder improvised not_run 'no board yet' (r-000016); the stand-in's board review found the Work section showed states but no verdicts, so two fail verdicts were invisible (r-000045); the fast builder planned its own items with no record of the planner lane.
lesson: small-model trials surface every unstated edge case as an improvisation; each improvisation a builder had to make is a missing sentence in the seed

text: Seed 1.1.1 (PATCH, wording only): S-0-07 foreign files (foreign row with pattern, tool, first_seen; excluded via .gitignore only after a ruling yes; never deleted without a yes; interview asks once, topic foreign); S-0-05 patterns in words; S-0-04 and S-0-08 not_run 'no board yet' only before cut 1's first step 08; WORK.md blocked-verifier rule (verifier prints its row, executor appends it verbatim with appended_by, actor stays the verifier) and planner_lane; START step 03 names the frontier planner and planner_lane: fast; BOARD.md Work lists every verdict row per item.
